title: Trace Export Health and Swallowed Flush Errors
dataSources: `SplunkAOLogger.export_health` (`ExportHealth(healthy, consecutive_failures, last_failure)`) and the error callback passed to `flush(on_error=callback)`
description: Watches whether the Splunk Agent Observability receiver is acknowledging the agent's trace export, using `logger.export_health` and a `flush(on_error=...)` callback, so export failures reach the agent's own logs instead of being swallowed.
value: Without a callback, flush errors are logged as a warning and swallowed, so an expired token or unreachable endpoint can stop all tracing unnoticed. Surfacing them lets the team fix the credential before the gap matters.
implementation: After each `flush()` in batch jobs, and periodically in long-running services, read `logger.export_health` and pass an `on_error` callback to `flush`. Log or alert from the application when `healthy` is false or `consecutive_failures` rises.
visualization: Application log line or health endpoint field showing export health and consecutive failures.
knownFalsePositives: `export_health` reports whether the receiver acknowledged data. It does not report traces dropped for having no spans (see UC-13.8.2), so a healthy value does not prove every request was recorded.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

`logger.export_health` returns `ExportHealth(healthy, consecutive_failures, last_failure)`. `flush(on_error=callback)` surfaces flush errors; without the callback they are logged as a warning and swallowed.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Nothing to configure in the console. Expose the health value through the application's own logs or health endpoint.

Step 3 — Validate

Point a test process at a wrong `SPLUNK_AO_API_URL` and confirm the callback fires and `healthy` turns false. Restore the setting and confirm it recovers. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Alert from the application's existing monitoring when `consecutive_failures` keeps rising. In batch jobs, check health after the final `flush()` and fail the job if export failed.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Credential error on SaaS: check `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`. On on-prem, check `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY`; the SDK derives the API host by replacing `console` with `api` in `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`, and `SPLUNK_AO_API_URL` is only needed when that derivation is wrong.
grandmaExplanation: We check that the notes the assistant writes are actually reaching the place that stores them, and shout if the delivery keeps failing.

productArtifacts.title: Surface export failures from the logger
productArtifacts.body:
import logging

log = logging.getLogger("agent.tracing")

def on_flush_error(err):
    log.error("Splunk Agent Observability flush failed: %s", err)

logger.flush(on_error=on_flush_error)

health = logger.export_health  # ExportHealth(healthy, consecutive_failures, last_failure)
if not health.healthy:
    log.error("trace export unhealthy: %s consecutive failures, last: %s",
              health.consecutive_failures, health.last_failure)
